transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lydia Moore (Zenith Head of ML), Carlos Gutierrez (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): walk through batching and KV/prefix cache recommendations, show cost-savings scenarios, discuss latency budget and POC next steps.

[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava with redwood, i'll hand it to samir for the deep dive \u0014 quick context, this is the optimize walkthrough focused on batching and caching and the cost model.
[00:18] Samir Patel: hey all, hi \u0014 uh Lydia, Carlos, Priya \u0014 thanks for the time. we'll go through a couple concrete traffic patterns, show how prefix vs kv cache behaves, and then run through a handful of cost scenarios. any specific must-haves before i start?
[00:30] Lydia Moore: yeah \u0014 main things: we do sessioned chat for financial advisors, average session length is about 6 turns, mean tokens per request ~450, we have p95 latency goal 350ms, and security's got strict KMS + audit log needs.
[00:48] Priya Shah: correct, and encryption at rest + key ownership, also data residency EU. we need proof-of-concept before legal signs off.
[00:58] Ava Chen: perfect, thanks. Samir, over to you.
[01:05] Samir Patel: ok quick slide \u0014 batching basics: larger batch_size improves throughput/cost but increases latency. example numbers (approx): batch size 1 = 90ms per request on our hosted M model, batch size 8 = 220ms median but token cost per inference drops ~3x. these are illustrative \u0014 we'll run your traffic to get exact.
[01:32] Carlos Gutierrez: when you say token cost drops, is that because of kernel amortization or kv cache reuse?
[01:38] Samir Patel: mostly kernel amortization for the forward pass when we batch many in a single GPU step; caching (prefix/KV) helps by avoiding re-computation of earlier tokens for session history. both stack.
[01:50] Lydia Moore: can you explain prefix vs kv cache again, specifically for our 6-turn sessions?
[01:56] Samir Patel: sure. prefix caching stores the encoded prefix on the serving node so repeated prefixes are re-used when identical \u0014 good for repeated prompts or system messages. KV cache stores key/value attention states per session so you only compute delta tokens at each turn. in session chat, KV cache usually gives best latency for long histories because you avoid recomputing the whole context each turn. prefix cache is cheaper when many users share the same initial prompt or system prompt.
[02:25] Ava Chen: note \u2014 terminology in eng teams can vary, sometimes prefix is called prompt cache, and kv is called attention cache; transcripts may have those words swapped.
[02:35] [crosstalk] Priya Shah: okay \u2014 and how does this map to our cost model \u2014 we sent you a spreadsheet earlier but it's high-level.
[02:42] Samir Patel: yeah, quick cost math: assume model cost per token on hosted M variant is $0.0008 per 1k tokens (example), with kv cache enabled per-session you save X% of tokens processed \u2014 in practice for your 6-turn average and 450 tokens/request we saw 40-60% token reduction on similar customers. if we further batch during peak we can reduce GPU utilization cost by another 20-30% but watch latency.
[03:10] Lydia Moore: 40-60% is a wide range \u2014 what's driving variance?
[03:14] Samir Patel: session length distribution, how often users are returning to the same session, and whether system prompts are large. also whether you do partial-message streaming (affects batching). in our benchmarks, with 6-turn sessions and heavy repetition in system prompt we saw ~55% average token avoid, but with highly diverse freeform user content it's closer to 35-40%.
[03:40] Carlos Gutierrez: for dedicated deployment \u2014 if we go Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity \u2014 does caching live on dedicated nodes and survive restarts?
[03:50] Samir Patel: yes, on Dedicated we persist KV caches to local persist store for active sessions and we have strategies for warm-up \u2014 still depends on your SLA for restarts. for Private on-prem, KV store can be backed by your infra (Redis/HBM) depending on config.
[04:05] Priya Shah: speaking of security \u2014 how do you handle KMS/keys for KV cache encryption?
[04:10] Samir Patel: KMS integrates with customer KMS/HSMs via our key wrapping. KV cache blobs are encrypted at rest per-customer key and audit logs show access events. we'll send our integration notes but plan is client-managed keys for Private/Dedicated, hosted can use Redwood-managed with options for BYOK.
[04:28] Ava Chen: noted \u2014 send SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes as a follow-up.
[04:33] [00:04:33] Lydia Moore: i have a question about batching windows \u2014 what's the typical latency tradeoff if we allow, say, a 30ms batching window vs 100ms?
[04:44] Samir Patel: 30ms window gets small micro-batches \u2014 you see modest throughput increase, little token savings. 100ms provides significantly larger batches at peak, about 2-3x token efficiency improvement in GPU utilization, but p95 latency can jump 50\u2013120ms depending on model. because you're already at 350ms p95 budget, you can afford a small batching window but not a long one during interactive flows.
[05:12] Carlos Gutierrez: is there an automated policy to only batch during non-interactive steps? like between retries or background processing?
[05:18] Samir Patel: yes \u2014 Redwood Optimize provides dynamic batching policies: latency-aware batching that adapts to your route SLOs, plus background batch lanes for low-priority work. we can tune thresholds per-route.
[05:28] [pause for screen share as Samir pulls up cost workbook]
[05:35] Samir Patel: ok i'm sharing the workbook \u2014 high level we modeled three scenarios: Hosted with KV cache + small batching, Hosted without cache, and Dedicated reserved with aggressive batching + KV caching. here's the assumptions: sample traffic 10k queries/day, avg tokens per query 450, session reuse 40%, reserved capacity 1x A100-equivalent.
[05:58] Lydia Moore: can you walk the numbers for hosted+kv?
[06:02] Samir Patel: sure. hosted + kv + 50% token avoidance = effective tokens processed per query = 225. at 10k q/day that's 2.25M tokens/day or ~67.5M tokens/month. at $0.0008 per 1k tokens that's about $54/month in model compute cost \u2014 these are illustrative numbers \u2014 plus infra markup, request overhead, etc.
[06:28] Priya Shah: wait $54/month seems low \u2014 are we missing something? that number only covers raw model token compute; we also include network egress, request handling, and infra margins. in the workbook we add a 4x multiplier to approximate total billable units, so that'd be ~$216/month.
[06:43] Samir Patel: correct, we include request overhead and per-request ingress/egress. also when you go Dedicated, you pre-commit to capacity \u2014 the unit economics shift: upfront cost but predictable throughput and often lower per-token effective cost at scale.
[06:56] Carlos Gutierrez: what about tail latency if we do a hybrid strategy \u2014 cache on sessions but route some traffic to a cheaper model for non-critical flows?
[07:05] Samir Patel: intelligent routing can do that \u2014 route best-effort / low-risk flows to smaller quantized models and critical flows to higher-accuracy models. Redwood's optimizer will pick kernels/quant levels per-route. caching helps all tiers but KV cache is most effective on large models with big context.
[07:23] [08:00 marker \u2014 mid call, discussion continues about POC logistics]
[08:05] Lydia Moore: for the benchmark we want to replicate our peak traffic pattern \u2014 500 qps for 2 minutes bursts and otherwise 20 qps baseline; can Redwood replicate that?
[08:15] Samir Patel: yes, we can run a benchmark harness against a staging endpoint or your Dedicated test cluster. we usually do a 48-hour run with both synthetic and replayed traffic to capture variability. we'll include throttling patterns and a cold-start test for KV warm-up.
[08:32] Ava Chen: we'll prepare a runbook for the benchmark \u2014 Samir, you'll lead on the perf scenarios.
[08:38] Samir Patel: yep. i'll propose three bench scenarios: steady-state baseline, burst spike, and long-session heavy-history. each reports latency p50/p95/p99 and token processing breakdown and cost per 1000 requests.
[08:52] Priya Shah: also include audit log verification and KMS key rotation tests during POC.
[08:58] Samir Patel: noted \u2014 we'll include compliance checks.
[09:02] [09:02] Carlos Gutierrez: small nit \u2014 you mentioned persisting KV cache for Dedicated, do you have an expected memory footprint per active session? we need to know infra sizing.
[09:11] Samir Patel: rough rule of thumb: KV cache size scales with context length and model hidden size \u2014 for our M-class model we estimate ~60\u2013120KB per 1k tokens of context. so for a 3k token session you might see ~180\u2013360KB. multiply by concurrent sessions to size. we'll send you a more precise table based on your average context.
[09:34] Lydia Moore: interesting. if sessions are 3k tokens and we have 10k concurrent sessions that's a lot of memory. how do you handle eviction?
[09:42] Samir Patel: we provide LRU eviction and checkpointing strategies; also you can tier cold sessions to Redis-backed store (slower but cheaper) and keep hot sessions in GPU or local RAM. tradeoffs again.
[09:56] [10:00] Ava Chen: this part is often the surprise for platform teams \u2014 we'll highlight tiering strategies in the deck we send.
[10:05] [10:15] Lydia Moore: going back to cost model \u2014 can you show a simple example that contrasts Hosted vs Dedicated numerically for our numbers?
[10:22] Samir Patel: yes. Hosted: example monthly effective tokens (after kv) 67.5M -> cost base $54 (raw) * 4 = $216 plus per-request overhead -> final estimate $320/month. Dedicated: assuming you reserve a single GPU-equivalent at $X/month \u2014 (example) reserved capacity might be $3,000/month but supports much higher QPS; amortized per-query cost at our volume could go down to $0.05 per 1k tokens effective. At your current 10k q/day this isn't yet at the breakpoint, Dedicated starts to make sense above ~200k q/day in our model.
[10:56] Priya Shah: that's the key \u2014 our current usage is lower but expected to grow; would you recommend starting hosted then POC with reserved capacity sizing?
[11:04] Samir Patel: yes common approach: start hosted to validate product and collect traffic, then run a Dedicated sizing exercise as you approach break-even. for the POC we can run a Dedicated sizing simulation so you know where the economics flip.
[11:16] Lydia Moore: how much data do you need from us for the POC?
[11:20] Samir Patel: minimal: 48h sample traffic with timestamps, payload sizes, tokens per request, session ids, and an expected concurrency profile. plus security checklist. we can work with anonymized payloads for compliance.
[11:32] Ava Chen: action items recap \u2014 we'll send cost model, runbook, SOC2 + KMS notes, and schedule the follow-up. who should own the POC internal at Zenith?
[11:42] Lydia Moore: i'll own ML metrics and evaluation, Carlos will own infra and platform, Priya will sign off on compliance.
[11:49] Ava Chen: great.
[11:52] [12:00] Quick QA: 
[12:05] Carlos Gutierrez: what if we want to use a third-party KV store like redis cluster for session persistence \u2014 supported?
[12:11] Samir Patel: yes \u2014 we have configs for Redis-backed sessions; performance lower than in-memory but cheaper and easier to scale.
[12:18] Lydia Moore: can you do partial KV snapshotting to S3 for cold sessions?
[12:22] Samir Patel: yep, snapshot to object store is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we use internal blob store encrypted with KMS.
[12:31] [12:40] Priya Shah: any regulatory gotchas with cross-region replication of KV cache? we need EU-only residency.
[12:46] Samir Patel: we can pin cache/storage to EU regions on Dedicated/Private. Hosted can also be region-constrained but requires contract-level assurances; we'll note residency options.
[12:58] [13:00] Closing recommendations from Samir (paraphrased):
- Start with hosted + KV cache enabled, small batching window (<= 50ms) for interactive flows to stay within 350ms p95.
- Use prefix cache for standard system prompts to reduce early-token compute.
- Enable background batching lanes for low-priority work and non-interactive routes.
- Run 48-hour POC benchmark with your traffic to validate real token avoidance and tail latency.

[13:31] Ava Chen: yes \u2014 we'll send both.
